statement: For a stationary simple locally finite planar point process of finite positive intensity, with bounded Voronoi cells, finite nonempty Delaunay neighbor sets, unique nearest nuclei at deterministic observation points and general position, define F6(x) as the average of exp(6i arg(q-p_x)) over Delaunay neighbors q of p_x. Let C6 be its centered complex covariance, V(t) the empty-disk probability, and alpha(A,B) the supremum of event-covariance magnitudes for the restrictions to A and B. Then for every r>0 and deterministic x,y, |C6(x,y)| <=16 alpha(B(x,3r),B(y,3r))+28 V(r/32).
assumptions: stationary simple locally finite planar process with finite positive intensity
bounded Voronoi cells and finite nonempty edge-neighbor sets
general position and unique nearest nuclei
spatial nearest-cell observable; no Palm conditioning
proof_or_counterexample: Seven-disk shielding gives a local bounded approximation with L1 error at most 7V(r/32), using a union bound without independence. Complex local covariance is bounded by 16alpha. Four L1 replacement errors give 28V. Full proof: BRIDGE_PROOF.md G1-G3.

statement: For independent uniform signs H and (A_k,B_k), let the three variables in block k be A_k,B_k,H A_k B_k. Every distinct variable pair is independent, but products of all three variables in distinct blocks have covariance 1 and the strong event-mixing coefficient of the two complete block sigma fields equals 1/4. Thus pair decorrelation alone does not imply full local-event mixing.

discrete block process; no asserted Riesz or point-process realization
